findings.text: the gained commit rewrites apply_section_dependency_edits in a file outside the node's declared write paths, so reckon crew check --manifest refuses the run at promotion until the grant is extended or the extract is re-dispatched to a node that owns the file; the edit itself is equivalence-preserving — the mapping is still judged by _read_section_dependency_mapping and passed in by mapping=, so the unreadable-value refusal stands — and it was made on the earlier review's explicit instruction to give both maps one editor, which the reviewer should record as an authorised scope extension rather than a defect of the change.

edit_keyed_meta is now the shared owner of the section-dependency write too, but the node's gate runs only tests/test_a_descope_is_written_on_any_plan.py and tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py, so a regression in the shared editor on the dependency route would pass this gate; the pre-existing tests/test_section_edge_summary_and_malformed_mapping.py and tests/test_section_edge_stays_off_plan_blocking.py cover it and were not in either arm.

the fragment states 28 ruff findings over 'the two edited modules' at the base and the same 28 at this node, but the node now edits three modules (reckon/_store_section_ops.py joined them) and the figure 28 is the line count of --output-format=concise, which includes ruff's own summary lines — the earlier review measured 26 findings — so the sentence names the wrong module count and a count that is not the finding count.
